prompts.A: A student investigates how the wavelength of light shone on one side of the shoot affects the response of bean seedlings. The table shows the mean angle of stem curvature toward the light source after 24 hours (mean ± 2SE) for each group of bean seedlings. Identify the independent variable in the investigation.
prompts.B: Identify the group that served as the control in the investigation, and explain why a control group is needed.
prompts.C: State a null hypothesis for the investigation.
prompts.D: A student claims that blue light increases the angle of stem curvature toward the light source compared with white light (control). Using the data in the table, support the student's claim.

input.design_note: Part A adds a brief description of the table (no numbers changed); all other parts keep the original wording with no answers revealed.

prompts.A: Based on the data in the table, describe the relationship between pH and the mean initial reaction rate of the amylase-catalyzed reaction across the three pH levels.
prompts.B: Calculate the percent change in the mean initial reaction rate from pH 4 to pH 7. Show your work.
prompts.C: Using the error bars (±2SE) reported in the table, identify the pair of pH levels, if any, for which the mean initial reaction rates are not statistically different. Justify your answer.
prompts.D: A student claims that the initial reaction rate of the amylase-catalyzed reaction is greatest at pH 7. Use the data to support the claim, and describe what the error bars (±2SE) indicate about the claim.

input.design_note: Four-part data analysis of a table of mean initial rates ±2SE at three pH levels, covering trend description, percent change calculation, interpretation of 2SE error bars, and evidence-based claim support.

prompts.A: A student investigates how the relative humidity of one half of a two-choice chamber affects the response of pill bugs (isopods). The table shows the mean number of pill bugs (out of 20) found in the test half of the chamber after 10 minutes for each group (mean ± 2SE). Identify the independent variable in the investigation.
prompts.B: Identify the group that served as the control in the investigation, and explain why a control group is needed.
prompts.C: State a null hypothesis for the investigation.
prompts.D: A student claims that 90% increases the number of pill bugs found in the test half of the chamber compared with 60%. Using the data in the table, support the student's claim.

input.design_note: Wording only polished; all numbers and group labels from the table are unchanged, and a brief setup sentence was added to Part A without altering any quantities.

prompts.A: A group of students measured the volume of oxygen released by a catalase-catalyzed reaction at three temperatures. The table shows the mean oxygen released in 2 minutes (milliliters) ± 2SE at 10 °C, 37 °C, and 70 °C (n = 12 for each temperature). Based on the data, describe the relationship between temperature and the oxygen released in 2 minutes across the three levels.
prompts.B: Calculate the percent change in the mean oxygen released in 2 minutes from 10 °C to 37 °C. Show your work.
prompts.C: Using the error bars (±2SE), identify the pair of temperature levels, if any, for which the mean oxygen released in 2 minutes is not statistically different.
prompts.D: A student claims that the oxygen released in 2 minutes is greatest at 37 °C. Use the data to support the claim, and describe what the error bars indicate about it.

input.design_note: Four-part data-analysis bundle on catalase activity vs. temperature: describe trend, calculate percent change, interpret ±2SE error bars, and evaluate a claim with evidence.
